description: Microsoft SQL Server 2022 health metric catalog.
release_notes: v1.2.1 (2026-09-23): catalog maturity label added (draft: not yet reviewed by a technology leader, neither for collection nor for scoring). No metric, threshold, weight or rule change. v1.2.0: schema-ready for consistency_rules (rules deferred to Technology Leader work). v1.1.0: Subcategory point allocations within Capacity, Performance, and Future-Proofing pillars differ from the architecture specification (SCORING_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md section 2.3). These splits have been stable since v1.0.0 and are flagged for tech-leader review. See docs/guides/metric-placement-review.md for details.

metrics.description: Whether the database recovery model is FULL. Required for transaction log backups and point-in-time recovery.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET RECOVERY FULL; then take a full backup to initialize log chain

metrics.description: Frequency of transaction log backups for FULL recovery databases. Backups every 60 minutes or less limit data-loss exposure.
metrics.remediation: Schedule transaction log backups at least every hour using SQL Server Agent or Maintenance Plans

metrics.description: Transaction log backup success over the last 24 hours. Failures break the log chain and prevent point-in-time recovery.
metrics.remediation: Check SQL Server Agent job history and msdb.dbo.backupset for failed log backups

metrics.description: Transaction log growth control. Sudden 50%+ growth signals a stalled log chain, long transactions, or AG sync issues.
metrics.remediation: Check log_reuse_wait_desc in sys.databases; ensure log backups are running and VLF count is managed

metrics.description: Virtual Log File (VLF) count for the transaction log. High VLF counts (>1000) slow recovery and log backups.
metrics.remediation: Shrink and grow log file in large increments to reduce VLF count

metrics.description: Whether a regular full backup schedule exists (weekly minimum). Without it, recovery options are limited to ad-hoc backups.
metrics.remediation: Configure SQL Server Agent job or Maintenance Plan for regular full backups

metrics.description: Age of the most recent successful full backup. Backups older than 7 days indicate stalled or failing backup jobs.
metrics.remediation: Check msdb.dbo.backupset for recent full backups; verify SQL Agent jobs are succeeding

metrics.description: Whether differential backups run between full backups. Reduces restore time and storage by limiting log replay.
metrics.remediation: Add differential backup jobs (daily) between weekly full backups to shorten restore time

metrics.description: Whether backups are validated with RESTORE VERIFYONLY. Catches corrupt or unrestorable backups before they're needed.
metrics.remediation: Add RESTORE VERIFYONLY step to backup jobs or use Ola Hallengren backup solution

metrics.description: Whether 'backup compression default' is on. Reduces backup size and I/O during BACKUP and RESTORE.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'backup compression default', 1; RECONFIGURE;

metrics.description: Whether backup files are encrypted. Required to protect sensitive data on backup media and offsite copies.
metrics.remediation: Use WITH ENCRYPTION option in BACKUP DATABASE command or use TDE + backup to encrypted media

metrics.description: Whether an enterprise backup framework (Ola Hallengren, Redgate, or commercial) is in use rather than ad-hoc scripts.
metrics.remediation: Consider Ola Hallengren's Maintenance Solution (free) for enterprise-grade backup management

metrics.description: Whether msdb backup history is retained long enough for reporting and audit. Aggressive cleanup hides backup gaps.
metrics.remediation: Ensure msdb cleanup jobs (sp_delete_backuphistory) do not purge too aggressively

metrics.description: Whether a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is documented. Drives backup frequency and replication design.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RPO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Whether a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is documented. Drives HA topology and restore procedure choices.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RTO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Whether the restore procedure has been exercised in the last 90 days. Untested restores often fail when needed.
metrics.remediation: Schedule regular restore tests to a non-production environment at least quarterly

metrics.description: AG backup preference setting. SECONDARY/PREFER_SECONDARY offloads backup I/O from the primary replica.
metrics.remediation: Set AG backup preference: ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP [agname] SET (AUTOMATED_BACKUP_PREFERENCE = SECONDARY_ONLY);

metrics.description: Sync state of the AG secondary replica. Required for failover readiness and offload reads.
metrics.remediation: Check sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states for AG health; investigate network and log send queue

metrics.description: Whether backup retention meets organizational policy (minimum 7 days of full backups). Required for compliance and rollback windows.
metrics.remediation: Configure backup retention in your backup solution to meet compliance requirements

metrics.description: Whether an offsite copy of backups exists. Protects against site loss; required for most DR plans.
metrics.remediation: Configure backup copy jobs to Azure Blob, S3, or secondary site

metrics.description: Whether backup storage capacity is monitored with alerts. Full backup volumes silently break the backup chain.
metrics.remediation: Configure disk space monitoring on backup volumes with alerting

metrics.description: Authentication mode. Windows Authentication leverages Kerberos/AD and avoids SQL password management.
metrics.remediation: Use Windows Authentication Mode where possible for Kerberos/AD integration

metrics.description: State of the 'sa' login. Should be disabled or renamed; default sa is a high-value target for brute-force attacks.
metrics.remediation: ALTER LOGIN sa DISABLE; or rename to a non-default name

metrics.description: Whether login attempts are audited (at minimum failures). Required to detect credential-stuffing and brute-force activity.
metrics.remediation: Configure SQL Server Audit for login success/failure events

metrics.description: Whether SQL logins enforce CHECK_POLICY/CHECK_EXPIRATION. Without it, weak passwords and stale credentials can persist.
metrics.remediation: ALTER LOGIN [loginname] WITH CHECK_POLICY = ON, CHECK_EXPIRATION = ON;

metrics.description: Presence of orphaned or unused SQL logins. Stale accounts widen the credential attack surface.
metrics.remediation: Review and remove unused SQL logins; use sp_change_users_login to fix orphaned users

metrics.description: Whether Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) protects at-rest data in sensitive databases. Required for compliance regimes covering PII/PHI.
metrics.remediation: Enable TDE: CREATE DATABASE ENCRYPTION KEY WITH ALGORITHM = AES_256; ALTER DATABASE ... SET ENCRYPTION ON;

metrics.description: Whether Force Protocol Encryption is on so all client connections use TLS. Required to protect credentials and query payloads in transit.
metrics.remediation: Enable Force Encryption in SQL Server Configuration Manager; configure valid SSL certificate

metrics.description: Whether Always Encrypted is used for PII/sensitive columns. Keeps decryption keys outside the database engine.
metrics.remediation: Evaluate Always Encrypted for columns storing PII (SSN, credit cards, etc.)

metrics.description: Whether the Database Master Key (DMK) is backed up and stored securely. Lost DMKs make TDE/encryption-protected data unrecoverable.
metrics.remediation: Backup master key: BACKUP MASTER KEY TO FILE = '...' ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = '...';

metrics.description: Minimum TLS version required by the server. TLS 1.0/1.1 contain known weaknesses; TLS 1.2+ is the modern baseline.
metrics.remediation: Disable TLS 1.0/1.1 via Windows registry settings; enable TLS 1.2 minimum

metrics.description: Whether a SQL Server Audit specification exists and is running. Required for forensic record of security-relevant events.
metrics.remediation: Create server-level SQL Audit for FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP, SUCCESSFUL_LOGIN_GROUP, and DDL changes

metrics.description: Whether DDL changes (CREATE/ALTER/DROP) are captured by SQL Audit. Required to track schema drift and unauthorized changes.
metrics.remediation: Add SCHEMA_OBJECT_CHANGE_GROUP and DATABASE_OBJECT_CHANGE_GROUP to audit specification

metrics.description: Whether sysadmin and permission-change events are captured by audit. Required to detect privilege escalation and role tampering.
metrics.remediation: Add SERVER_PERMISSION_CHANGE_GROUP, SERVER_ROLE_MEMBER_CHANGE_GROUP to server audit

metrics.description: Storage and ACLs of the audit log target. Audit data on shared/world-readable paths can be tampered with or exfiltrated.
metrics.remediation: Store audit files on dedicated volume with permissions restricted to SQL Server service account

metrics.description: C2 audit mode state. C2 mode shuts the instance down when its trace volume fills; SQL Audit is the supported alternative.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'c2 audit mode', 0; RECONFIGURE; — use SQL Audit instead

metrics.description: Number of sysadmin role members. Bloated sysadmin membership widens blast radius and breaks least-privilege.
metrics.remediation: Remove unnecessary members from SysAdmin role; use least-privilege roles instead

metrics.description: Whether BUILTIN\Administrators is excluded from the sysadmin role. Membership grants every local OS admin DB superuser rights.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_dropsrvrolemember 'BUILTIN\Administrators', 'sysadmin';

metrics.description: Server-level state of cross-database ownership chaining. When on, it lets a database escalate privileges across databases.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'cross db ownership chaining', 0; RECONFIGURE;

metrics.description: User databases with TRUSTWORTHY ON. TRUSTWORTHY combined with high-privileged owners is a known privilege-escalation vector.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET TRUSTWORTHY OFF; — use signing for cross-database access instead

metrics.description: State of xp_cmdshell. When on, T-SQL can execute arbitrary OS commands as the SQL service account.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 0; RECONFIGURE;

metrics.description: Data file fill ratio. Exceeding 85% without headroom risks autogrowth stalls and out-of-space failures.
metrics.remediation: Pre-grow data files to avoid auto-growth events; monitor with sys.dm_db_file_space_usage

metrics.description: Whether data/log file autogrowth uses fixed MB rather than percentage. Percentage growth scales unpredictably and causes I/O storms.
metrics.remediation: Set autogrowth to fixed MB: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] MODIFY FILE (NAME='...', FILEGROWTH=512MB);

metrics.description: TempDB file layout. Multiple equally-sized files (up to 8) reduce allocation contention on busy workloads.
metrics.remediation: Add TempDB data files equal to number of logical CPUs (max 8); use trace flag 1117/1118 for older versions

metrics.description: Transaction log fill ratio. Exceeding 80% indicates a log_reuse_wait issue or insufficient log backups.
metrics.remediation: Check log_reuse_wait_desc; ensure log backups are running for FULL recovery model databases

metrics.description: Free space on the database volume. Below 20% headroom raises the risk of autogrowth failures and outages.
metrics.remediation: Monitor disk space via SQL Server DMVs or OS monitoring; archive/purge old data

metrics.description: Active connections relative to max worker threads. Approaching the limit causes new connections to wait or fail.
metrics.remediation: Monitor sys.dm_exec_sessions; consider connection pooling at application tier

metrics.description: Whether applications connect through pooled drivers (ADO.NET/JDBC/ODBC). Avoids connection storms and excess login overhead.
metrics.remediation: Ensure application framework connection pooling is enabled and correctly sized

metrics.description: Max worker threads setting. 0 (auto) or a CPU-aware override prevents thread starvation under load.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'max worker threads', 0; RECONFIGURE; (let SQL Server auto-configure)

metrics.description: Blocked process threshold setting. A non-zero value (<=5s) emits blocked-process reports for investigation.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'blocked process threshold', 5; RECONFIGURE;

metrics.description: Index fragmentation level. Above 30% degrades range scans and bloats buffer pool usage.
metrics.remediation: Schedule index rebuild/reorganize jobs (Ola Hallengren recommended); monitor sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats

metrics.description: Statistics freshness. Stale stats produce poor cardinality estimates and bad query plans.
metrics.remediation: Enable AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS; schedule manual UPDATE STATISTICS for large tables

metrics.description: Recency of a clean DBCC CHECKDB run. Without regular integrity checks, on-disk corruption can spread silently.
metrics.remediation: Schedule weekly DBCC CHECKDB; review MSDB.dbo.suspect_pages for corruption

metrics.description: Whether AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS_ASYNC is on. Avoids synchronous stats updates blocking critical query compilations.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS_ASYNC ON;

metrics.description: Database PAGE_VERIFY mode. CHECKSUM detects torn writes and on-disk corruption at read time.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET PAGE_VERIFY CHECKSUM;

metrics.description: Database compatibility level versus engine version. Lagging compat levels miss optimizer improvements.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET COMPATIBILITY_LEVEL = 160; (for SQL Server 2025)

metrics.description: Whether 'max server memory' is bounded below the OS total. The default leaves no headroom for the OS and other services.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'max server memory', [total_RAM_MB - OS_reserve_MB]; RECONFIGURE;

metrics.description: Whether MAXDOP is explicitly set. The default (0) lets a single query consume every scheduler and starve others.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'max degree of parallelism', [appropriate_value]; RECONFIGURE; (typically half of NUMA node CPUs)

metrics.description: Cost threshold for parallelism. Default of 5 over-parallelizes trivial queries; raising the threshold avoids wasted CXPACKET waits.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'cost threshold for parallelism', 50; RECONFIGURE;

metrics.description: log_reuse_wait_desc value. Anything other than NOTHING/LOG_BACKUP signals a stalled log chain (open tx, replica lag, etc.).
metrics.remediation: Investigate log_reuse_wait_desc in sys.databases; address open transactions or AG sync issues

metrics.description: Plan cache hit ratio. Below ~95% indicates frequent hard compiles, often from ad-hoc unparameterized queries.
metrics.remediation: Increase plan cache size (max server memory); use parameterized queries; enable Optimize for Ad Hoc Workloads

metrics.description: Page Life Expectancy. Sustained PLE under ~300s per 4GB NUMA node signals memory pressure.
metrics.remediation: Increase max server memory; investigate large table scans; review buffer pool extension

metrics.description: Whether 'optimize for ad hoc workloads' is on. Avoids storing full plans for one-off queries that bloat the plan cache.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'optimize for ad hoc workloads', 1; RECONFIGURE;

metrics.description: Whether Buffer Pool Extension on SSD is in use when RAM is constrained. A stopgap when physical memory cannot be increased.
metrics.remediation: Consider BPE on NVMe SSD if physical RAM cannot be increased

metrics.description: Whether the compat level enables Intelligent Query Processing (Memory Grant Feedback, batch-mode-on-rowstore, etc.).
metrics.remediation: Set compatibility level >= 150 (SQL Server 2019) to enable IQP; use QUERY_OPTIMIZER_COMPATIBILITY_LEVEL hint

metrics.description: Whether Query Store is on for user databases. Required for plan history, regression detection, and forced plans.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET QUERY_STORE = ON (OPERATION_MODE = READ_WRITE);

metrics.description: High-impact missing-index recommendations from sys.dm_db_missing_index_details. Frequent recommendations point to schema/query gaps.
metrics.remediation: Review sys.dm_db_missing_index_group_stats; implement high-impact missing indexes after testing

metrics.description: Whether any critical wait type (PAGEIOLATCH, RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE, CXPACKET) dominates the wait profile.
metrics.remediation: Review sys.dm_os_wait_stats; address top waits (memory pressure, I/O, parallelism, locking)

metrics.description: Queries in Query Store whose average duration exceeds 60s. Persistent slow queries usually need a plan or index fix.
metrics.remediation: Use Query Store Top Resource Consuming Queries report; apply query hints or plan forcing if needed

metrics.description: Whether the Query Store Regressed Queries report is reviewed regularly. Catches new plans that perform worse than prior ones.
metrics.remediation: Review Query Store Regressed Queries; use sp_query_store_force_plan for critical plan stabilization

metrics.description: Database parameterization mode. SIMPLE fits most OLTP; FORCED helps workloads with heavy ad-hoc SQL.
metrics.remediation: Evaluate FORCED parameterization for OLTP workloads with many ad-hoc queries

metrics.description: Whether AUTO_CREATE_STATISTICS is on. Without it, the optimizer lacks column-level statistics needed for good plans.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET AUTO_CREATE_STATISTICS ON;

metrics.description: Presence of long-lived blocking chains in sys.dm_exec_requests. Persistent chains stall throughput and time out waiters.
metrics.remediation: Investigate blocking head using sys.dm_exec_requests; review long-running transactions and index design

metrics.description: Deadlocks captured by the system_health XE session in the last 24 hours. Recurring deadlocks point to lock-ordering or design issues.
metrics.remediation: Enable trace flag 1222 or use system_health XE session to capture deadlock graphs; fix lock ordering

metrics.description: Whether RCSI or Snapshot isolation is on. Cuts reader/writer blocking but adds tempdb version-store load.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON; (requires tempdb space for version store)

metrics.description: Lock Pages in Memory privilege state. Recommended for OLTP servers where the OS may page out the buffer pool.
metrics.remediation: Enable LPIM Windows privilege for SQL Server service account on OLTP servers with high memory pressure

metrics.description: AG log send queue size in seconds of data. Sustained growth signals network or secondary I/O bottlenecks.
metrics.remediation: Check sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states log_send_queue_size; investigate network bandwidth

metrics.description: AG redo queue (log received but not yet applied to secondary). High redo queues delay failover RPO and read-only workloads.
metrics.remediation: Increase redo thread parallelism; check secondary disk I/O performance

metrics.description: Whether the AG has a synchronous replica with FAILOVER_MODE = AUTOMATIC. Required for hands-free HA failover.
metrics.remediation: Configure synchronous replica with FAILOVER_MODE = AUTOMATIC for HA scenarios

metrics.description: Transactional replication distributor-to-subscriber latency. Sustained latency >30s indicates an unhealthy distributor or subscriber.
metrics.remediation: Check Replication Monitor for latency; review distributor transaction count and agent performance

metrics.description: Major SQL Server version. Out-of-support versions stop receiving security and stability updates.
metrics.remediation: Plan upgrade to SQL Server 2019 or 2022; SQL Server 2014 reached end of support

metrics.description: Recency of the applied Cumulative Update. CUs older than ~6 months miss security patches and bug fixes.
metrics.remediation: Download and apply latest CU from Microsoft Update Catalog; test in non-production first

metrics.description: Time remaining before mainstream support ends. Less than 12 months requires an active upgrade plan.
metrics.remediation: Review Microsoft SQL Server support lifecycle page; plan upgrade timeline

metrics.description: Whether applied CUs and hotfixes are tracked in change management. Required for audit, rollback, and incident triage.
metrics.remediation: Maintain patch history in CMDB or change management tool

metrics.description: Whether an Always On AG or FCI is deployed for HA. Without one, an instance failure means manual recovery.
metrics.remediation: Deploy Always On AG for read-scale and HA, or FCI for shared-disk failover clustering

metrics.description: Whether the SQL service account has Perform Volume Maintenance Tasks. Required for instant file initialization on data file growth.
metrics.remediation: Grant 'Perform Volume Maintenance Tasks' to SQL Server service account; restart SQL Server

metrics.description: Whether the Dedicated Administrator Connection is reachable. Provides a recovery channel when normal connections are blocked.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'remote admin connections', 1; RECONFIGURE; to enable remote DAC

metrics.description: Whether a documented SQL Server upgrade plan exists. Without it, end-of-support arrives as a surprise.
metrics.remediation: Plan upgrade using Microsoft Upgrade Advisor or Database Experimentation Assistant (DEA)

metrics.description: Hits on deprecated features in sys.dm_os_performance_counters. Deprecated usage blocks future upgrades.
metrics.remediation: Query sys.dm_os_performance_counters WHERE object_name LIKE '%Deprecated%'; fix before upgrading

metrics.description: Surface area exposure from optional features (OLE Automation, CLR, ad-hoc distributed queries). Each one widens the attack surface.
metrics.remediation: Disable unused features: Ole Automation Procedures, CLR, Ad Hoc Distributed Queries via sp_configure

metrics.description: Whether DEA or MAP Toolkit has been used to assess upgrade impact. Catches workload regressions before the upgrade lands.
metrics.remediation: Download Microsoft DEA from GitHub and run workload comparison analysis before upgrade

metrics.description: Number of linked servers. Each linked server widens the trust boundary and complicates upgrades and security review.
metrics.remediation: Review and remove unused linked servers; avoid linked servers to production systems where possible

metrics.description: State of system_health and other diagnostic XE sessions. Without them, blocking and deadlock evidence is lost.
metrics.remediation: Ensure system_health XE session is running; create additional sessions for performance troubleshooting

metrics.description: Whether SQL Agent alerts cover critical conditions (I/O errors 823/824/825, drive space, job failures). Required for proactive incident response.
metrics.remediation: Configure SQL Server Agent alerts for severity 19-25 errors and I/O error codes 823, 824, 825

metrics.description: Query Store retention window. Less than 30 days makes plan-regression and trend analysis unreliable.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE [dbname] SET QUERY_STORE (DATA_FLUSH_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 900, CLEANUP_POLICY = (STALE_QUERY_THRESHOLD_DAYS = 30));

metrics.description: Whether architecture diagrams and operational runbooks are current. Outdated docs slow incident response and onboarding.
metrics.remediation: Maintain up-to-date architecture diagrams, runbooks, and change log

metrics.description: Number of databases using SIMPLE recovery. SIMPLE forfeits log backups and point-in-time recovery.
metrics.remediation: Consider FULL recovery model for production databases

metrics.description: Total transaction log file size on disk. Used to track growth trends and capacity planning.
metrics.remediation: Monitor log file growth; ensure regular log backups

metrics.description: Databases without a full backup in the last 24 hours. Any gap means at least one database is unrecoverable.
metrics.remediation: Schedule full backups for all production databases

metrics.description: Server-level authentication mode. Windows-only mode disables SQL logins and removes a credential-management surface.
metrics.remediation: Change to Windows Authentication mode via SQL Server Configuration Manager

metrics.description: State of 'clr enabled'. CLR loaded code runs in-process; should be off unless an application explicitly needs it.
metrics.remediation: Disable CLR: EXEC sp_configure 'clr enabled', 0; RECONFIGURE;

metrics.description: Whether any data file still uses percentage-based growth. Percentage growth scales unpredictably under heavy writes.
metrics.remediation: Change data file growth to fixed size: ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY FILE (FILEGROWTH = 256MB)

metrics.description: Whether 'optimize for ad hoc workloads' is on. Avoids storing full plans for one-off queries that bloat the plan cache.
metrics.remediation: EXEC sp_configure 'optimize for ad hoc workloads', 1; RECONFIGURE;

metrics.description: Maximum read latency on database files. Above ~20ms typically indicates I/O contention or storage saturation.
metrics.remediation: Investigate high disk latency — consider faster storage (SSD/NVMe) or reducing I/O pressure

metrics.description: Service pack and cumulative update level reported by the engine. Used to compare against the latest available CU.
metrics.remediation: Apply the latest Cumulative Update for your SQL Server version
